summary: Siuslaw NF lookout in Lincoln County, Oregon: an L-4 cab from the early 1930s, a 41-foot tower put up in 1954, and the tower removed after the 1970 fire season.

facts.design: 41-foot treated timber L-4 tower (1954) with an L-4 cab; the first L-4 cab dates to the early 1930s
facts.status_note: Tower removed after the 1970 fire season per Rex's page; the register says only that it has since been removed, and firelookout.com gives no removal date

staffing.status: staffed through 1970 per Rex's page; Lookout Irvin Hussey at the post in February 1943 per The Oregonian

events.note: The register dates the first L-4 cab to the early 1930s; the earliest dated record is a September 1931 Forest Service plan for a fireman's cabin, with project approval on September 12, 1931
A garage was built at the site
Activated March 18, 1942, listed under the Portland Filter Center
Lookout Irvin Hussey named in a February 1943 Oregonian story about a shooting reported from the post
A 41-foot treated timber L-4 tower with a cab was erected; Rex's page gives the estimated cost as $4,252
Final year the lookout was staffed
Tower removed after the 1970 fire season per Rex's page; no other source gives a removal year

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says only that the tower has been removed, and firelookout.com's header reads 'R.I.P. 1930's-1954; 1954-?' with no end date. Rex's page is the only source that dates removal, to after the 1970 fire season, so the 1970 year rests on that one page.

sources.title: Cougar Mountain
sources.publisher: Forest Lookouts (Oregon), Rex's Fire Lookout Page

notes_for_editor: Brief record is accurate (gone, Siuslaw NF, Lincoln County, 556 m). The 1970 removal year comes from Rex's page alone; the register and firelookout.com do not date it. The register's 'early 1930s' cab date is the only build date in the brief's sources; 1931 is the earliest dated plan. An Oregon Digital photo of the lookout (Siuslaw collection, pz50gw173) was not read because the fetch tool reported an SSL certificate error. No site-today description exists in any source read.
